# onpager_escalation_rule (Resource)

Manage one team's CEL escalation rule, target escalation chain and active state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_escalation_rule" "example" {
  team_id    = var.team_id
  name       = "Route production"
  cel_source = "false"
  chain_id   = var.chain_id
  active     = true
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}

variable "chain_id" {
  description = "Existing active escalation chain UUID valid for this team."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cel_source` (String) CEL condition source selecting this rule. Supply the expression directly, without JSON encoding.
- `chain_id` (String) Explicit escalation-chain UUID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `name` (String) Nonempty rule name without leading or trailing whitespace.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Desired active state, published atomically with content. Defaults to `true`. Inactive definitions remain readable and in state; a later apply reconciles this setting.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `revision` (Number) Latest published revision. Rule publication does not use If-Match.

## Import

Import using `team_uuid/rule_uuid`. Inactive definitions can be imported; a
later apply reconciles their content and `active` state.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_escalation_rule.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/88888888-8888-4888-8888-888888888888"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_escalation_rule.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/88888888-8888-4888-8888-888888888888
```

## Lifecycle

Publication saves the CEL expression, explicit escalation-chain binding and
active state atomically in a new revision. Writes have no revision precondition.
Priority and structured conditions are not supported.

Activation requires an active owner and a valid escalation chain. Publishing
inactive content is permitted under an inactive owner with the disable grant.
Refresh and import read the latest publication directly, including inactive
definitions.

Destroy disables the rule and preserves its configuration and history. It does
not unlink dependent definitions or archive the target chain. A failed disable
retains state.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `escalation_rules.read`, `escalation_rules.create`,
`escalation_rules.update` and `escalation_rules.disable`. Publishing inactive
content additionally requires the disable grant.
